title: Israeli Airstrike Kills Two, Including a Girl, in Al-Nasr Neighborhood of Gaza City
detail: An Israeli airstrike struck a vehicle in the al-Nasr neighborhood of western Gaza City on Sunday, September 6, 2026, killing two people, including a girl, and wounding six others, according to Mohamed Abu Selmia, head of Al Shifa Hospital, Gaza's largest hospital. The Israeli military had not commented on the strike as of publication. Hamas contends Israel is breaching the October 2025 ceasefire and obstructing implementation of President Trump's peace plan, which calls for an eventual Israeli withdrawal and Hamas disarmament. Gaza health officials say more than 1,300 Palestinians, predominantly civilians, have been killed since the ceasefire took effect, while Israel reports four soldiers killed in the same period.

media.caption: Israeli airstrike hits a vehicle in the al-Nasr neighborhood of western Gaza City, killing two, Sep 6, 2026

title: Gaza City Holds Mass Funeral for 100 People, Including 60 Children, Recovered from Rubble
detail: Palestinians in Gaza City held funeral ceremonies on Sunday, September 6, 2026, for approximately 100 people, including 60 children and 55 members of the Malaka family, whose remains were recovered from the rubble of destroyed buildings in the Zeitoun neighborhood. The remains were carried to al-Ma'madani cemetery for burial. Gaza civil defence head Raed al-Dahshan said 'We don't have equipment, we don't have protective equipment' for rescue workers, while UN human rights official Ajith Sunghay said 'Thousands of people are still languishing under this rubble.' An estimated 8,000 more bodies are believed still buried under rubble strip-wide. Gaza's Health Ministry puts the cumulative death toll since October 2023 at 73,651.

media.caption: Mass funeral held in Gaza City for 100 people, including 60 children, recovered from Zeitoun rubble, Sep 6, 2026

title: Eight Muslim-Majority Nations Warn of 'Grave Consequences' Over Israeli Gaza Displacement Plans
detail: The foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Jordan, the UAE, Qatar, Pakistan, Indonesia, and Turkey issued a joint statement on Sunday, September 6, 2026, strongly condemning proposals by Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz and National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir to remove Palestinians from Gaza. The statement said such 'inflammatory statements and proposals flagrantly violate principles of international law, including international humanitarian law, and pose a direct threat to the legitimate and inalienable rights of the Palestinian people,' and warned of the 'grave consequences of transforming calls for forced displacement into declared policy or practical measures.' The ministers said the proposals 'directly challenge international efforts to achieve peace, particularly President Donald Trump's comprehensive plan to end the conflict in Gaza, which includes a firm rejection of forced displacement.' The statement follows Katz's September 2 remarks that Israel is 'organised and prepared' to facilitate emigration, and Ben Gvir's September 3 'Disengagement 710' plan targeting removal of Gaza's roughly 2 million residents over seven years.

media.caption: Foreign ministers of eight Muslim-majority nations condemn Israeli plans to displace Gaza's population, Sep 6, 2026

title: Netanyahu Boasts of Bombing Qatar, Defends Transfer of Qatari Funds to Gaza
detail: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in an i24NEWS interview broadcast Sunday, September 6, 2026, referring to Israel's September 9, 2025 strike on Doha that killed five Hamas members and a Qatari security officer during ceasefire negotiations: 'I attacked Qatar, I also bombed it and attacked them during the war,' describing Qatar as a 'hostile' state that does not influence Israeli Gaza policy. Israel formally apologized to Qatar over the strike alongside President Trump in the aftermath. Netanyahu separately defended the transfer of millions of dollars in Qatari-funded aid to Gaza, which domestic critics allege helped enable Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack, saying the transfers were humanitarian, recommended by Mossad and Shin Bet, and amounted to '2 percent of all the money that entered the Strip.' Qatar's Sheikh Mohammed has said the funds 'went to Gaza, went to the people, and was under a very transparent process.' The remarks come weeks ahead of Israel's October 27 elections, with Netanyahu facing domestic pressure over Gaza war management.

media.caption: Netanyahu says he 'attacked Qatar' and defends Gaza aid fund transfers in i24NEWS interview, Sep 6, 2026
